planner_heuristic_statement: The historical audit operates on a strict multi-layer epistemic framework: raw historical facts -> semantic interpretations -> truth decisions. Requirement lifecycle (origin, evolution, active survival, or partial/full supersession) and implementation state (implemented, unenforced, partially represented, or missing) are treated as orthogonal dimensions. Historical Git commits, prompts, and nonce run artifacts serve as empirical evidence of requirement provenance, runtime behavior, and supersession; they are never assumed to be the normative goal. The normative implementation target is exclusively determined by what the machine existing today actually executes, orchestrates, and deterministicly validates across its Node.js source, GitHub Actions workflows, configuration files, and persisted schemas. An outstanding defect constitutes present corrective work if and only if the underlying user requirement survives un-superseded and today's executable machine fails to fully enforce it.
